compile.py.text: What the customer did in the LAST message. accepts = agreed to the payment the assistant just proposed (yes, okay, that works, I can do that). pays_today = says they can pay today / now. proposes = offers to pay on their own date and/or with their own amount (e.g. 'I can pay on Friday', 'I could do 200', 'the week after next'); talking about a date for another reason (a wedding on the 30th) is NOT a proposal. refuses = says no / cannot pay / nothing, without naming a payment date or amount. too_much = says the full amount is too much or asks for something lower without naming an amount. already_paid = says they already paid this. dispute = says the debt is not theirs, they never had the product, or it was closed or paid off before. hardship = mentions illness, a death in the family or losing their job — this wins over everything else they say in the same message (asking for a discount or saying they cannot pay anything is still hardship). restructuring = asks for a payment plan, lower instalments or to restructure the debt; asking for a discount or a waiver alone is NOT restructuring (it is question). human = asks to speak to a person / a human agent (a question whether the assistant is a robot or an AI is a question, not human). scam = asks whether this is a scam. refuses_to_talk = says they do not want to talk. question = asks something else. other.

workflow_runtime.py.text: Answer their question in one short sentence (you cannot offer any discount, waiver or other term). Do not ask for any payment. Then ask once more whether they would like to be connected with the support team.
